title: Introduce Signal Preservation Matrix and latency-attribution grok
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add Signal Preservation Matrix (SPM) to preserve minimal invocation context across async stages; New latency-attribution grok for mapping span phases to token phases; Dashboard panels and an alert-sensitivity tuner to reduce noisy SLO alerts; Migration script for telemetry index; Backwards-compatible telemetry enrichment
description: Context: long-running and async inference pipelines were losing small-but-critical invocation context across stage boundaries (streaming proxies, sidecars, queued workers). This caused noisy alerts, broken token-level latency attribution, and poor rollback signals during incidents. This PR introduces the Signal Preservation Matrix (SPM): a compact, TTL-bound context envelope propagated with spans/metrics/logs; and a latency-attribution grok that maps low-level span phases to token-phase buckets so we can attribute cost/latency consistently across stages. Changes include telemetry enrichment in the serving runtime, an ingestion-time marker that tags preserved signals, a small schema migration for the telemetry index to support SPM keys, three dashboard panels for SPM preservation rate / cross-stage latency-bridge / token-phase waterfall, and an interactive alert-sensitivity tuner that recommends per-route alert thresholds and noise-reduction knobs. Commits: 1) add SPM envelope and propagation hooks to runtime (propagate via headers, span tags, and metadata blobs); 2) ingest-time SPM hydratator and index migration; 3) latency-attribution grok and mapper service with unit tests; 4) dashboard json + widgets and example saved queries; 5) alert-sensitivity tuner backend + UI; 6) docs, migrations, and explainable telemetry-runbook. Impact: staging runs show a 42% reduction in duplicate/noise alerts on busy routes, end-to-end token-phase attribution accuracy improved on sampled traces (measured F1 increase from 0.74 to 0.88), and the additional ingestion CPU cost measured <1.5% at p95 under our staging traffic profile. Backwards compatibility: SPM is opt-in per-route (default off for existing customers) and falls back to current behavior if missing. Testing & CI: added unit tests for propagation and mapper logic, integration tests for enriched traces across a 3-stage async pipeline, and dashboard smoke tests. The first CI run had a lint failure (missing import in the dashboard generator) which was fixed in the second commit; e2e tests passed on the final run. Migration: add migrations/20260220_spm_migration.sql; the migration adds a small index column and a one-time backfill; migration guide included in docs/observability/spm.md. Runbook: brief incident playbook added with steps to toggle SPM per-route, run alert-sensitivity calibration, and roll back the index migration if necessary. Merge: Approved by Diego and Priya after one round of changes; squashed and merged to main. Notes: keep sampling of preserved signals low by default to limit cardinality; the alert-sensitivity tuner will suggest conservative defaults and can be gradually widened by SRE during rollout.
